name: fly-on-the-wall-cab
style: observational documentary field recording, real ambulance crew at night, spoken dialogue only, dry close-miked voices, ragged breath between words, British paramedics, understated not acted, minimal electronic underscore: low sub-bass hum, patient monitor beeps as the pulse, siren far off sliding past outside, rain on metal roof, tension without melody, voices sit on top, ends on a single sine tone then dead silence
exclude: singing, choir, chorus, melody, hook, orchestral, strings, epic trailer, cinematic hits, drums, comedic, upbeat, reverb-heavy vocals, rap
lyrics:
[Spoken, no singing. Inside the cab, rain, monitor beeping under sub-bass hum, siren far off outside]
[Woman paramedic, low and steady, starting to crack]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Man paramedic, quiet, quick]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Driver, off-mic from the front seat]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Siren cuts, engine idles, beeps keep going]
[Man paramedic, suddenly loud]
Why have we stopped?!
[Through a car window, posh, bored, nasal]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Woman paramedic, almost a whisper]
Fifty over twen—
[Music stops. Flatline: one pure sine tone]
[Silence]
[End]
